description: Inside the commerce services: record processing, retries and dead letters, consumer rebalances, the applied controlboard configuration, franz-go client metrics and the Go runtime.

panels.description: Records finished by the selected services (all results).
panels.title: Records processed / s

panels.description: Records produced and acknowledged by the selected services (franz-go).
panels.title: Records produced / s

panels.description: Retried batches per minute (database, produce, transient and schema registry errors).
panels.title: Retries / min

panels.description: Consumer group membership changes (assigned/revoked/lost) in the time range. Each rebalance pauses consumption briefly.
panels.title: Rebalances (window)

panels.description: Pods whose consumer is paused by the 'Silent Failure' knob of the controlboard.
panels.title: Paused consumers

panels.description: Applied control snapshot generation per service. All services should show the same number shortly after a change on the controlboard; a lagging service did not apply the latest settings.
panels.title: Control generation

panels.description: Records finished per second by service and result: ok, duplicate (skipped idempotently) and dlq (dead-lettered).
panels.title: Records processed by result

panels.description: Handler time per record (95th percentile, VictoriaMetrics histogram). Includes database work; compare with database transaction time below.
panels.title: Processing time p95 per record

panels.description: How old an event is when a service processes it (now − occurredAt): end-to-end freshness including Kafka lag. Rising age with stable processing time = the consumer is lagging.
panels.title: Event age at processing p95

panels.description: Time from polling a partition batch to committing its offsets (95th percentile).
panels.title: Batch duration p95 (poll → commit)

panels.description: PostgreSQL transaction duration per service (95th percentile). Slow transactions slow down every consumer that writes state.
panels.title: Database transaction time p95

panels.description: Retried batches per minute by service and reason (db, produce, transient, registry).
panels.title: Retries by reason

panels.description: Records dead-lettered per minute by service, topic and reason.
panels.title: Dead-lettered records by service

panels.description: Partition assignment changes per service: assigned, revoked, lost (lost = the member was kicked out, e.g. after a session timeout).
panels.title: Rebalances by kind

panels.description: Partitions each pod owns per topic. Uneven numbers mean uneven load between replicas of a service.
panels.title: Partitions assigned per pod

panels.description: Numeric knob values the services applied from the controlboard (only non-default knobs are exported), and Tuning Lab client rebuilds.
panels.title: Applied controlboard knobs

panels.description: Records and bytes produced per second by topic (acknowledged batches).
panels.title: Produce throughput

panels.description: Records per produce batch by topic. Small batches (≈1) cost broker CPU; tuning linger/batch size on the controlboard changes this line.
panels.title: Average records per produce batch

panels.description: Records fetched per second by topic (before processing).
panels.title: Fetch throughput

panels.description: Write+read time of requests per broker as seen by the clients (99th percentile). Compare with the broker-side request time on Broker Deep Dive: a gap means network or client-side queuing.
panels.title: Broker request latency p99 (client view)

panels.description: Connects, connect errors and disconnects per minute by broker node. Connect errors during a broker outage are expected; constant churn is not.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Records buffered in the clients waiting to be produced or processed, and broker throttle time (quotas).
panels.title: Buffered records and throttling

panels.description: Orders per second the generator should produce (controlboard) and actually produces, by kind (normal, duplicate, poison, hot).
panels.title: Generator target vs actual rate

panels.description: 1 while the generator cannot keep up with its target rate (Kafka is pushing back).
panels.title: Generator lagging

panels.description: Go heap in use and the soft memory limit (80 % of the container limit). Heap close to the limit makes the GC run continuously.
panels.title: Memory: heap in use vs GOMEMLIMIT

panels.description: Goroutines per service. A steadily growing number is a leak.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: Time spent in Go GC pauses per second (stop-the-world).
panels.title: GC CPU and pauses
